source.title: Pre-training under infinite compute
source.authors: Konwoo Kim; Suhas Kotha; Percy Liang; Tatsunori Hashimoto

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests batch-size effects on held-out performance using language-model pre-training and continued pre-training, with settings and measures that differ from the image-classification and language-model comparisons named in V5.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a batch-size ablation in Figure 13 and a continued-pretraining comparison in Table 1. The figure's exact values are not available in the text. Other optimizer, regularization, scaling, and downstream results do not directly test the listed versions; cited prior-work results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V5 in Llama-style language-model pre-training and continued pre-training: batch size varies while data and epoch budgets remain fixed, and outcomes are held-out validation loss or benchmark accuracy. It is not an original source for V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for batch size: smaller batches improve performance at fixed data exposure in the tested settings. The paper's broader conclusion is that epoching, tuned regularization, parameter scaling, ensembling, and distillation improve data efficiency when compute is abundant. Its infinite-compute performance estimates are extrapolated scaling-law asymptotes.
record.recipe_differences: The batch-size comparisons use Llama-style language-model pre-training and continued pre-training, rather than the image-classifier settings in V5. The continued-pretraining batch comparison uses 512 versus 64 and holds the epoch count at one; other recipe details differ across cited studies and are not fully comparable.
record.method_sensitivity: The batch-size result is described for a fixed number of data points; the practical minimum was batch size 64 on their hardware. In continued pre-training, the lower-batch comparison is at one epoch and 4B tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing transformer parameter count eventually raises validation loss under the standard recipe, while jointly tuning weight decay, learning rate, and epochs restores monotone improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under fixed language-model data budgets, the relationship between parameter count and held-out loss depends on regularization and training hyperparameters.

record.code_released: https://github.com/konwook/lm-eval-ensemble; the paper also states that runs and code were open-sourced, but gives no training-code URL in the supplied text.
record.problems: The pre-training batch-size ablation's numerical values are only in Figure 13, and the supplied text does not provide them. The continued-pretraining batch comparison is one setting and the overall recipe's gains also include other interventions; no uncertainty is stated for Table 1.
record.rows_left_out: No additional directly relevant batch-size outcome is separately stated in the supplied text. Other model-scaling, weight-decay, distillation, ensemble, and downstream-benchmark results do not measure a version's named behavior or intervention.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No isolated width sweep beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold in unregularized one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.
No adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparison.

Does not locate a critical batch size or test whether longer training, batch-specific learning-rate scaling, warmup changes, normalization, or regularization adaptations remove the larger-batch penalty.
Dropout is explicitly not considered or tuned.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or ranking of generalization-gap predictors.
No identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Table 6 isolates batch size for the continued-pretraining comparison; epoching and ensembling gains should not be attributed to that intervention. R2 averages R3–R5 and is not independent evidence. No uncertainty is reported for these batch comparisons. The parameter-scaling findings do not test V2 because model depth and width both change, regularization is present, and an interpolation threshold is not established.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label versus random-label comparison.
Does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU networks or whether test error rises or falls beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparison.
Uses AdamW but does not compare adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers.
Does not establish the workload-dependent critical batch size or compare broad large-batch recipes, including the cited warmup, normalization, and regularization adaptations.
No dropout intervention or dropout ablation.
Does not measure sharpness or compare it with other generalization measures.
Does not identify and remove memorized training examples.
